new_entities.name: Peanut introduction at 4 to 6 months in high-risk infants
aliases: early peanut introduction in high-risk infants
new_entities.description: Introducing peanut-containing foods during the 4 to 6 month window in infants at elevated risk of peanut allergy.

new_entities.name: Peanut allergy prevention
new_entities.description: Lower risk of developing IgE-mediated peanut allergy.

edges.effect_quant: In the LEAP randomized trial, early peanut consumption in 640 high-risk infants was associated with an 86% reduction in peanut allergy among those with a negative baseline skin-prick test and a 70% reduction among those with mild baseline sensitization.
edges.population: infants at high risk of peanut allergy, especially those with severe eczema, egg allergy, or both
edges.mechanism: Early oral peanut exposure during infancy may promote immune tolerance and counteract cutaneous sensitization pathways in high-risk infants.
edges.summary: Introducing peanut during the 4 to 6 month window in high-risk infants is strongly protective against later peanut allergy. This is one of the clearest food-allergy prevention findings in pediatrics.
edges.caveats: High-risk infants may need individualized introduction plans, especially if already sensitized. The evidence is strongest for supervised or guideline-based early introduction rather than unsystematic exposure.

evidence.citation: Burgess JA et al 2019 Clin Exp Allergy
evidence.notes: Age at introduction to complementary solid food and food allergy and sensitization: A systematic review and meta-analysis.

evidence.notes: Randomized trial of peanut consumption in infants at risk for peanut allergy.
